messages.subject: poisson_log problem/ rstan debugging
parts:
Using the development code, from rstan, the compiler complains

TRANSLATING MODEL 'stan_model' FROM Stan CODE TO C++ CODE NOW.
Error in stanc(file = file, model_code = model_code, model_name =
model_name, :
failed to parse Stan model 'stan_model' with error message:
EXPECTATION FAILURE LOCATION: file=input; line=34, column=52

nDetail[n] ~ poisson_log(beta_x[n]) T[1, 15];
^-- here


DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:
no matches for function name="poisson_log_cdf_log"
arg 0 type=int
arg 1 type=real
available function signatures for poisson_log_cdf_log:
lower truncation not defined for specified arguments to poisson_log
Parser expecting: <eps>

Am I doing something wrong, or is this a bug? I put the full code at
the bottom.

BTW, I tried a vectorized version of the nDetail ~ poisson... above, but
it said I couldn't vectorize when using truncation.

Also, is there a good way to double check that my calculations are doing
what I think they should? I'd like to make sure that my matrix
operations are acting as I expect. I see there is a print statement,
but am not sure if that works from rstan. Is there some way I could
capture some of the calculation and pass it back out?

I marked the line that most concerns me below:
data {
int<lower=0> N; // number of respondents
int<lower=0> J; //number of covariates
int<lower=0> NSD; // number of classes of beta for sd
int<lower=1,upper=NSD> SDClass[J]; // beta[j, k] has
sigma_beta[SDClass[j]]
int<lower=0> NCLUSTER; //number of respondents
int iCluster[N]; // cluster id
matrix[N, J] x; // covariates
int<lower=1,upper=15> nDetail[N]; // outcome
}
parameters {
vector[J] beta_raw; // standard covariate coefficients
vector[NCLUSTER] alpha_raw; // cluster effects
real<lower=0> sigma;
real<lower=0> sigma_beta[NSD];
}
transformed parameters {
vector[J] beta;
vector[NCLUSTER] alpha;
for(ir in 1:J)
beta[ir] <- beta_raw[ir]*sigma_beta[SDClass[ir]];
alpha <- alpha_raw*sigma;
}
model {
vector[N] beta_x;
sigma ~ cauchy(0, 5);
sigma_beta ~ cauchy(0, 5);
beta_raw ~ normal(0, 1);
alpha_raw ~ normal(0, 1);
for (n in 1:N) {
// would particularly like to check the next line
//also could it be vectorized as beta_x <-
(x*beta)+alpha[iCluster]?
beta_x[n] <- (x[n] * beta)+alpha[iCluster[n]];
//truncated poisson can't be vectorized
nDetail[n] ~ poisson_log(beta_x[n]) T[1, 15];
}
}"

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] poisson_log problem/ rstan debugging
parts:
Hi Ross,

Are you intending to use the log-parameterized poisson distribution?

A couple notes:
- We haven't truncated that distribution (yet). That's what the error message is trying to convey -- there isn't a truncation available for that distribution.
- If that is the intended distribution, for the time being, you can use:
nDetail[n] ~ poisson(exp(beta_x[n])) T[1, 15];
- We don't have vectorized truncation (yet). That's something we've got on our todo list.

I'm heading to bed now -- I'll let someone else respond on saving values.


Daniel

> Also, is there a good way to double check that my calculations are doing
> what I think they should? I'd like to make sure that my matrix
> operations are acting as I expect. I see there is a print statement,
> but am not sure if that works from rstan.

Yes, it works in RStan. You can always try things out
in tiny test models.

> Is there some way I could
> capture some of the calculation and pass it back out?

Anything declared as a transformed parameter is saved
along with the parameters.

We don't have any kind of testing framework in place,
but you can use "if" in the code to check for conditions
and print if you find them. For instance, calculate both
ways and use if to test and if different, print.
